title: The Institution of the Eucharist: Fifth Luminous Mystery
summary: Pray the Fifth Luminous Mystery page by page: the story of the Institution of the Eucharist, the Gospel, the decade prayers, and a quiet reflection.
coverAlt: Juanes's painting of the Last Supper: Jesus gives the bread and chalice to his apostles.

pages.title: The Institution of the Eucharist
pages.body: At the Last Supper, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and said: This is my body. He gave himself to us as food for the journey. As we pray this decade, we thank Jesus for the Eucharist and ask to love him more in Holy Communion.
pages.imageAlt: Juanes's painting of the Last Supper: Jesus gives the bread and chalice to his apostles.

evidence.claim: Original child-friendly meditation on the mystery; the mystery and its traditional day follow the standard Rosary order.

pages.title: From the Gospel
pages.body:
God's Word tells us this mystery. From the Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 26 (Douay-Rheims Bible):

“And whilst they were at supper, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and broke: and gave to his disciples, and said: Take ye, and eat. This is my body. And taking the chalice, he gave thanks, and gave to them, saying: Drink ye all of this. For this is my blood of the new testament, which shall be shed for many unto remission of sins.”

(Matthew 26:26-28)

evidence.claim: Scripture quotation reproduced word for word from the Douay-Rheims 1899 American Edition (public domain); verse numbers omitted for reading aloud and ellipses mark skipped verses.

pages.title: Praying the Decade
pages.body:
We announce the mystery: The Institution of the Eucharist, the Fifth Luminous Mystery. Then we pray one decade of the Rosary, holding this scene in our hearts.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen. (We pray the Hail Mary ten times, once for each bead of the decade.)

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell; lead all souls to Heaven, especially those in most need of Thy mercy.

evidence.claim: The Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be and Fatima prayers use the standard formulas printed across this site.

pages.title: The Fruit of This Mystery: Love of the Eucharist and sacrificial union
pages.body:
This mystery grows the fruit of love of the Eucharist and sacrificial union. Jesus gives himself to us as bread. How can you prepare your heart for your next Holy Communion?

Let us pray: Lord Jesus, Bread of Life, help us receive you with love and become bread for others. Amen. Our Lady of the Rosary, pray for us.

evidence.claim: Original reflection and closing prayer; the fruit of the mystery follows the traditional list used across this site.
